messages:
jordan: Heads-up — seeing intermittent 401s from the Kotlin client in prod starting ~10:30. Pattern: request A works, token refresh happens, then a batch of followups get 401s for ~30s. Anyone seen this?

maria: Hmm. OkHttp + interceptor ordering can cause stale headers if refresh updates a shared token but queued requests already built. Are we using an Interceptor for auth or an Authenticator? :thinking_face: 

jordan: We currently do an Interceptor that reads TokenProvider.get() and sets Authorization header. TokenProvider does an async refresh when it hits expiry.

rico: If you set header in an interceptor, requests that were already created (or in-flight) will keep the old header. Authenticator runs on 401 and can retry with new creds. Might be better for refresh-on-401 flow.

emily: Also check connection pooling reuse — if backend validates header per-connection (weird), keep-alive could reuse a conn with stale metadata? not common but possible.

jordan: Example interceptor we have:
```
val authInterceptor = Interceptor { chain ->
  val token = tokenProvider.get()
  val req = chain.request().newBuilder()
    .header("Authorization", "Bearer $token")
    .build()
  chain.proceed(req)
}
```

maria: That looks normal. If tokenProvider.get() returns old token until refresh finishes, you'll send old token. Two options: 1) make tokenProvider.blocking-refresh so get() blocks until new token available, or 2) use an Authenticator to handle 401s and refresh/ retry.

ankit: Authenticator pattern:
```
val authenticator = Authenticator { route, response ->
  val newToken = tokenRefresher.refreshBlocking()
  response.request.newBuilder()
    .header("Authorization", "Bearer $newToken")
    .build()
}
val client = OkHttpClient.Builder()
  .authenticator(authenticator)
  .addInterceptor(authInterceptor)
  .build()
```
Note: interceptor still sets header for normal requests; authenticator only kicks on 401 and retries.

jordan: If we do blocking refresh in get() that could add latency to a hot path. We prefer optimistic interceptor + authenticator fallback.

maria: Agreed. Also ensure your refresh code updates the token in a thread-safe way (volatile/atomic) so subsequent interceptor calls get the new value.

emily: Another subtlety: are you mutating the Request object somewhere else (e.g., earlier interceptor) and reorder of interceptors means Authorization gets overwritten later? Interceptor order matters: addInterceptor runs in the order added for application interceptors; network interceptors run later.

rico: Related tip: do not rely on connection-level metadata. OkHttp sends headers on the Request object; once request built it's final. If you update token after building, those in-flight ones won't change.

jordan: Also seeing one stack trace that looked like a ClassCast when parsing streaming responses (NDJSON). Error mentions gson vs jackson classes. Could shading be related?

maria: Yes — mixing Jackson streaming parser and Gson on the same payload can be fine, but classloading/shading issues cause NoClassDefFoundError or ClassCast. Are you bundling both libs? Is the client shaded?

emily: In our kotlin client we shaded Gson for the CLI but left Jackson as-is. If a transitive dep expects com.google.gson.stream.JsonReader and you relocated it, that will fail at runtime.

\ankit: For shadowing in Gradle use relocate to move package names. Example: 
```
shadowJar {
  relocate('com.google.gson', 'com.redwood.shaded.gson')
}
```
If you relocate, make sure nothing else needs the original package at runtime (or also relocate all consumers).

rico: Alternatively, avoid shading one of them — prefer a single JSON library on the classpath for the client runtime to minimize surprises. If you must mix, keep both on their original packages.

jordan: The NDJSON stream parsing oddity — sometimes the parser throws on a trailing CRLF chunk when using bufferedSource. Anyone used Okio.peek() safely for streaming?

emily: We use this pattern: 
```
val source = response.body!!.source()
while (!source.exhausted()) {
  val line = source.readUtf8LineStrict()
  // parse as JSON
}
```
Works with Jackson streaming or manual Gson from String. If you use readUtf8() instead you might consume partial frames.

maria: Also watch for using Jackson's ObjectMapper.readValues(source) vs readTree on partial chunks — the streaming reader expects well-formed JSON tokens. For NDJSON, parse line-by-line.

jordan: Thanks — good checklist. Action items for me:
- switch to interceptor + Authenticator pattern and make refreshBlocking() for authenticator only
- audit token provider for thread-safety and volatile/atomic update
- check gradle shadowJar relocations, remove partial shading of gson if needed
- change NDJSON parsing to readUtf8LineStrict + per-line parse

emily: +1 on those. Also add e2e test that simulates token expiry + concurrent requests to catch this before prod.

rico: If you want I can drop a small repro in a playground later today. :thumbsup:

jordan: That would be great. I'll post the trace and build.gradle in this thread shortly.

devops-bot: Deploy log: token-refresh-service v1.12 rolled back at 10:45 — flagged by error budget monitor.

jordan: Noted. Will coordinate with devops. Thanks y'all :pray:
